text:
devon_support: Customer (org_id=org_8f3c) reported their monthly credits showed 0 at 2024-11-09T06:10:22Z, expected reset at 08:00 UTC. They received 429s from API. Paste of customer curl/response (redacted):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' 
 -d '{"model":"gpt4o-mini","input":"hello"}'

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
{"error":{"type":"quota_exceeded","message":"monthly credits exhausted","remaining_tokens":0}}
```

They say the UI showed 0 credits starting ~06:05 and kept getting 429s until 08:12 when reset finally happened for them. Can infra/billing take a look? cc @pete_billing @tim_infra

pete_billing: Thanks, devon. Can you confirm tenant timezone and billing window on that org? Also any recent changes to refill logic?

devon_support: Tenant metadata: `billing_window_hour=8`, `billing_tz=UTC`. No customer-side timezone overrides. They are on hosted plan. No recent plan changes.

anya_prod: quick QA: did the UI cache or frontend show an older value? Could be display cache expiring early.

devon_support: I asked customer — they force-refreshed the console, still saw 0. They also repro'd with API so not just UI.

tim_infra: looking at refill job runs. Our refill controller log for today (times in UTC):
```
2024-11-09T05:59:58Z refill-controller: starting scan
2024-11-09T06:09:12Z refill-controller: queued tenant org_8f3c for refill
2024-11-09T06:09:13Z refill-controller: refill completed for tenant org_8f3c (credits_added=100000)
```
This explains why the customer saw refill at ~06:09. Why did controller run for an 08:00-window tenant? Investigating schedule translation.

credits-bot: [automation] Billing-refill job UUID=refill-20241109-06 completed 06:09:13Z. Affected: 12 tenants (list redacted).

pete_billing: Interesting. Our intended cron is `0 8 * * *` UTC for tenants with `billing_window_hour=8`. How did they run at 06? Any env var override deployed?

tim_infra: Found a recent config tweak in k8s deployments: `REFILL_CRON_OVERRIDE=0 6 * * *` was introduced in configmap cascade for the apac-ops K8sConfig but mistakenly applied to the refill-controller deployment in all namespaces during rollout. The rollout started last night and the controller picked it up this morning. That explains the 06:09 run.

anya_prod: Oof. That would shift many tenants with 08:00 windows earlier if the controller interprets override in local cluster TZ. But why only some tenants?

tim_infra: The controller applies override only when `USE_CLUSTER_CRON_OVERRIDE=true` in the configmap. The flag was flipped during the rollout for a targeted namespace but the configmap was cluster-scoped; due to an operator bug it propagated. So only controllers that reloaded the config picked it up — hence partial impact.

devon_support: Customer impact: a subset of tenants saw their monthly credits refill ~2 hours early, then other tenant groups saw the expected 08:00 refill. The affected customers reported 0 credits and 429s until their actual expected window passed; some were then refilled early causing confusion.

pete_billing: Action items: 1) revert the configmap change (done?), 2) identify affected tenants and notify, 3) verify no double-refill or charge issues. I can take 2/3.

tim_infra: Reverted `REFILL_CRON_OVERRIDE` and set `USE_CLUSTER_CRON_OVERRIDE=false` in the cluster configmaps at 06:45 UTC. Confirmed controllers reloaded and next scheduled refills are back to tenant-config cron (08:00).

devon_support: Customer wants explanation and assurance they won't be billed extra. I told them we are investigating and will follow up.

pete_billing: We check billing ledger: refill controller only grants the configured monthly credit amount once per calendar cycle. Because early run happened before cycle end for some tenants, for those affected the ledger shows the refill executed at 06:09 and the cycle advanced. No duplicate credits were issued later. For tenants that had no early run, normal 08:00 refill applied. No overcharging — only timing mismatch. We'll still notify affected customers and offer one-time courtesy credit for the confusion.

anya_prod: Can we add a safety: controller should refuse cluster-level override unless operator explicitly confirms `ALLOW_GLOBAL_CRON_OVERRIDE=true` in an admin-only namespace. Also add a canary rollout to prevent cluster-scoped config propagation.

tim_infra: Agreed. Filed infra ticket INFRA-870. Also added a post-deploy check: if `REFILL_CRON_OVERRIDE` changes, require manual approval.

credits-bot: [automation] Created ticket INFRA-870: "Prevent accidental cluster-scope refill cron override"

devon_support: I wrote a short customer-facing note for the affected orgs explaining root cause and compensation plan. Pete, will you coordinate formal customer messaging?

pete_billing: I'll send the batch notify and attach the ledger excerpt. Will offer a one-time credit and include a short technical note.

devon_support: Thanks all. Customer confirmed they received credits back and 429s stopped after our rollback. Marking this thread resolved. :white_check_mark:
